packages.label_en: The Tzaddik's Decree and the Priestly Blessing
packages.reason: The Torah's sole bechina equates the tzaddik who can decree — who says 'I say it shall be so' — with the formula of the Priestly Blessing: 'So shall you bless... say to them (אָמוֹר לָהֶם).' The shared essential nature is authoritative, reality-creating declarative speech by the holy person. The Kohen does not petition God to bless; he declares the blessing as an already-established fact. The higher tzaddik similarly does not request — he decrees. Both are two expressions of the same capacity: holy speech that is performative, not petitionary. This contrasts structurally with the ordinary tzaddik who petitions (בַּקָּשָׁה), whose request may or may not be heard — that mode belongs outside this package as the narrative foil.
